issues_detected.description: updates.frequency states a semi-annual (twice yearly) cadence, but the release history the record itself supplies is denser and irregular: 2025-01-17 (1.1), 2025-04-16 (2.0.0), 2025-08-18 (2.0.1), 2025-12-16 (3.0.0), 2026-05-01 (3.1.0) — five releases in roughly sixteen months. The record caveats that the cadence statement was written against Health Data Nexus hosting, but does not reconcile it with the observed PhysioNet release pattern.
issues_detected.recommendation: Restate the update cadence against the PhysioNet release history, or mark the semi-annual figure as a planning target rather than an observed frequency.

issues_detected.description: version_access.latest_version_doi is given as doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42, which related_datasets (relationship_type: is_version_of) identifies as the concept DOI resolving to the latest version. The DOI of the version actually described by this record is 10.13026/8xbn-nq66. A field named latest_version_doi holding a concept DOI is a slot/value mismatch that could mislead an automated consumer.
issues_detected.recommendation: Either record the resolved version DOI (10.13026/8xbn-nq66) in latest_version_doi, or rename/annotate the value explicitly as the concept DOI.

issues_detected.description: keywords contains only four broad terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice). No clinical condition (Parkinson's disease, ALS, laryngeal cancer, depression), no modality or method term (spectrogram, MFCC, acoustic features, speech), and no data-type term appears, despite all of these being prominent in the description and phenotype inventory. Searchability is materially weaker than the rest of the record would support.
issues_detected.recommendation: Extend keywords to at least 8-12 terms covering conditions, acoustic feature types, and study design, drawn from content already present in description and file_collections.

issues_detected.description: The dedicated download_url slot is unpopulated. Platform access is nonetheless locatable: distribution_formats.access_urls give https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ for both formats, raw_sources.access_url gives the Synapse controlled-access location, and license_and_use_terms states the credentialing steps.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate download_url with the PhysioNet content URL so machine consumers do not have to reach into distribution_formats.

issues_detected.description: at_risk_populations is not used; the vulnerable-population content lives in human_subject_research.special_populations (neurological/neurodegenerative cohorts including mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's, ALS, Parkinson's; mood and psychiatric cohorts including depression, bipolar, PTSD). The information is present and specific, but in a non-canonical slot.
issues_detected.recommendation: Mirror the special_populations content into at_risk_populations with the protections applied to each group.

issues_detected.description: content_warnings.content_warnings_present is false while a warnings entry is supplied. The record explains the pairing (the warning describes free-speech transcripts removed at 1.1 and excluded from the feature-only 3.0.0/3.1.0 releases), so the semantics are recoverable, but the boolean and the populated list read as contradictory to a consumer that reads only the flag.
issues_detected.recommendation: Move the superseded warning into a historical-notes field, or set the flag to reflect that a caveat text is carried.

issues_detected.description: confidential_elements_present is false while sensitive_elements_present is true, access is credentialed/restricted, a Certificate of Confidentiality applies, and the Data Transfer and Use Agreement characterizes the data as personally identifiable information under OMB M-07-16. The record flags the tension in source_caveats and scopes the false answer to the feature-only release, which makes the position defensible but not self-evidently coherent.
issues_detected.recommendation: State explicitly in confidentiality_details why doctor-patient-privileged content is absent from a release that is nonetheless credentialed and covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality.

issues_detected.description: sensitive_elements carries an acknowledged internal conflict: the healthsheet inventory lists race, sexual orientation, socioeconomic and health information as present, while the version 3.0.0 de-identification account states that all REDCap-flagged sensitive fields and highly sensitive non-identifying elements (household income, mental health status, traumatic life experiences) were removed. The record reports both rather than resolving which holds for 3.1.0.
issues_detected.recommendation: Resolve against the 3.1.0 file inventory: enumerate which sensitive attributes are actually present in the released phenotype tables.

issues_detected.description: variables enumerates only four elements (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames) for a release whose phenotype directory holds dozens of tables across confounders, demographics, eighteen diagnosis tables, enrollment and thirteen questionnaires. The record compensates by documenting that every table ships a companion JSON data dictionary carrying description, question text and data type.
issues_detected.recommendation: Either expand variables to cover the principal analytic columns, or add an explicit pointer field stating that the authoritative variable metadata is the distributed JSON data dictionaries.

issues_detected.description: conforms_to is deliberately omitted, with source_caveats explaining that the BIDS 1.9.0 conversion describes the audio dataset's folder layout rather than this feature-only release. The omission is honest, but it leaves no data-level community-standard conformance assertion for the released artifact; ICD-10 appears only as a labeling protocol and conforms_to_schema describes the datasheet, not the data.
issues_detected.recommendation: State any standard the released tables do follow (for example the phenotype/JSON data-dictionary convention, ICD-10 coding of diagnosis columns) in conforms_to, scoped to this release.

issues_detected.description: The RRID carried in the citation string (RRID:SCR_007345) is the resource identifier of PhysioNet, the hosting platform, not of the Bridge2AI-Voice dataset. The format is valid and the usage follows PhysioNet's own citation convention, but the identifier does not uniquely identify this dataset.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the platform RRID in the citation but note that dataset-level identification rests on the version DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66.

issues_detected.description: collection_timeframes supplies no start or end dates. The twelve-month figure is caveated as drawn from documentation written against versions 2.0.0/3.0.0, and the record itself observes that the cohort accumulated across releases from 306 to 833 participants, so the stated span probably does not describe the assembly of the released cohort.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record first and last collection dates for the 3.1.0 cohort, or state that they are unavailable from any source.

semantic_insights: DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 uses the PhysioNet prefix 10.13026, which matches the declared publisher (https://physionet.org/) and the citation — identifier, registrar and platform agree.

Grant identifiers 3OT2OD032720-01S1 and OT2OD032720 both parse as NIH awards (OT2 other-transaction activity code, OD = Office of the Director, serial 032720, supplement suffix -01S1), consistent with the stated NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI funder.

The human-subjects chain is complete and mutually consistent: involves_human_subjects=true, USF single-IRB approval with subsite approvals, prospective written/electronic/video informed consent with a documented withdrawal boundary, and participant compensation with explicit per-session amounts.

The deidentification method is appropriate to the data type and is the load-bearing design decision of the release: HIPAA Safe Harbor plus indirect-identifier removal, plus withholding the waveform itself because voice is biometric — the record releases derived features precisely in place of the identifying signal.

Re-identification risk is assessed rather than asserted away: the record states that voice remains unique to a person even after HIPAA identifiers are stripped, states that k-anonymity with k>=2 was not achieved, and names the mitigation (waveform exclusion, prohibition on re-identification attempts).

Sensitive-record handling is feature-specific rather than blanket: dense features (spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, PPGs, articulatory estimates) were withheld for free-speech and audio-check recordings while static features were retained, and the per-feature record counts (29,278 / 32,522 / 28,640 / 31,855 / 31,872 / 29,289) are reported unequal in a way that matches that account.

Bias documentation uses a recognizable taxonomy (selection_bias, representation_bias, measurement_bias, annotation_bias) and the measurement-bias entry identifies a real confound — cohort is entangled with site and therefore with recording device — which future_use_impacts then follows through to the modeling consequence (models may learn site or device signatures).

Processing is described at replicable granularity: 16 kHz monaural resampling with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter, STFT with 25 ms window / 10 ms hop / 400-point FFT, 60 MFCCs, SPARC articulatory traces at 50 Hz, PPGs over forty phoneme categories at 100 Hz, with b2aiprep pinned to version 3.0.0.
Release dates are temporally ordered and coherent with the record's own metadata: 2025-01-17 through 2026-05-01, with issued and last_updated_on (2026-05-01) matching the 3.1.0 release date.

The record distinguishes the two access tiers consistently across license_and_use_terms, third_party_sharing, regulatory_restrictions, raw_sources and external_resources: credentialed access to derived features on PhysioNet, controlled access to raw audio via Synapse behind DACO review and an institutional Data Transfer and Use Agreement.

Non-representativeness is declared in sampling_strategies (is_random false, is_representative false) and carried through consistently to known_biases, known_limitations and discouraged_uses, which explicitly discourages uses that assume representativeness.

Source conflicts are disclosed rather than silently resolved throughout (grant identifier variants, participant/target counts, language eligibility, access model across releases, cleaning-vs-healthsheet disagreement), with a declared source ranking and a preferred value stated each time.

overall_score.denominator_note: No sub-element was excluded: the datasets-shared condition is met (Parquet/TSV distribution formats with PhysioNet access URLs and a research-use license), the human-subjects condition is met (833 adult participants, clinical diagnoses), the governance condition is met (credentialed access, confidentiality_level restricted), the data-collection condition is met (acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms populated), and the software-output condition for Element 8 sub-element 3 is met (external_resources names code repositories). adjusted_max_points = 50 - 0 = 50; both percentages therefore share the denominator 50.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; id: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; citation carries 'RRID:SCR_007345'; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42 (concept DOI)
sub_elements.quality_note: A resolvable version DOI, a URI identifier, and a concept DOI for the version series are all supplied; identification is unambiguous at both version and series level.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: DOI matches 10.XXXX/... and the prefix 10.13026 is PhysioNet's, agreeing with publisher and citation. RRID matches RRID:SCR_XXXXX; SCR_007345 identifies PhysioNet (the platform) rather than the dataset, noted as a low-severity scope issue but not disqualifying since the DOI carries dataset-level identity.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description of roughly 1,700 characters naming 833 adult participants, five North American sites, four adult condition categories plus controls, the feature-only scope (spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, SPARC articulatory measures, PPGs, pitch contours, openSMILE/Praat/parselmouth static features), the phenotype directory contents, Parquet/TSV distribution, and the credentialed access condition
sub_elements.quality_note: Far beyond the 200-character threshold and semantically dense: the description states what is in the release, what is deliberately not (raw waveforms), how it was collected, and on what terms it can be obtained.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Description is internally consistent with instances (833), file_collections (feature/metadata/phenotype layout), distribution_formats (Parquet, TSV) and license_and_use_terms (credentialed). No drift between summary and structured fields.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: [health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice]
sub_elements.quality_note: Four keywords, below the five-term guideline, and all of them broad program- or domain-level terms. None names a condition (Parkinson's disease, ALS, laryngeal cancer, depression, chronic cough), a modality or feature type (spectrogram, MFCC, acoustic features, speech), a population (adult), or a study design — all of which are documented elsewhere in the record and would carry the retrieval load. Discovery by a user searching for, say, a dysphonia or neurodegeneration voice corpus would fail on these tags.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Terms present are relevant and correctly used; the failure is coverage, not correctness. The gap is measurable against the record's own phenotype inventory of eighteen conditions.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://b2ai-voice.org/; distribution_formats.access_urls: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; file_collections describes three named collections (features, metadata, phenotype) each with an id, path, collection_type and contents
sub_elements.quality_note: Both a project landing page and the platform content page are given, and the internal resource hierarchy is described down to individual file names and the phenotype subdirectory structure (confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaire, task).
sub_elements.semantic_validation: URLs are well-formed with plausible domains; the collection ids are constructed as fragments of the dataset URI, which is internally consistent.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_supplemented_by 10.13026/h995-bt35 (pediatric companion, 300 participants at SickKids); is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68 (version 3.0.0); is_version_of 10.13026/37yb-1t42 (concept DOI); derives_from syn72370534 (raw audio on Synapse)
sub_elements.quality_note: Four typed relationships, each with a resolvable target and substantive notes explaining what the related resource contains and how it relates. The derives_from edge to the withheld raw audio is the key provenance link for a feature-only release and is made explicit.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship types are used correctly and non-redundantly (version-of for the concept DOI, new-version-of for the immediate predecessor). parent_datasets is unused, but the same structural information is carried by the typed relationships.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: general_research_use; license_terms describing credentialed access under the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement, the separate controlled-access route for raw audio (Data Access Request Form, DUA, DACO review, institutionally signed DTUA), and the absence of non-commercial/geographic/research-type restrictions; ip_restrictions lists five specific terms including no transfer of IP rights, duplication permitted but sale prohibited, no IP claims that would block access, Fort Lauderdale Agreement adherence, and no third-party IP encumbrances
sub_elements.quality_note: Access policy and IP terms are both operationally specific: a prospective user learns exactly which credential and which signature are required, what may be duplicated, and what may not be sold or patented in a blocking manner.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Policy restrictiveness matches the sensitivity claims elsewhere (biometric voice data, Certificate of Confidentiality) without over-claiming: commercial research is explicitly permitted because the consent did not restrict it, which is consistent with informed_consent.consent_scope.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; regulatory_restrictions list ('No export controls apply', credentialed-access restriction, institutional sign-off for raw audio); other_compliance describing a Certificate of Confidentiality that must be asserted against subpoenas and the DTUA's characterization of the data as PII under OMB Memorandum M-07-16; governance contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org recorded in maintainers (Bridge2AI-Voice Consortium Data Access Compliance Office)
sub_elements.quality_note: Classification, export-control status, HIPAA status, an additional statutory protection, and a reachable governance contact are all present. The source_caveats candidly state that neither classification term is used verbatim by a source and explain the inference from PhysioNet's credentialed policy and the healthsheet's HIPAA answer.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Enum values are used correctly and cohere with the access policy. The governance contact sits in maintainers rather than data_governance.committee_contact; the substantive requirement (a contact for the responsible governance body) is met, with the slot placement noted.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats[].access_urls: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ (given for both the Parquet and the TSV distribution); raw_sources.access_url: https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; license_and_use_terms states the credentialing and agreement steps required to obtain the files
sub_elements.quality_note: The dedicated download_url slot is empty, but the sub-element asks for a download link or platform access instructions and both are present and actionable: the PhysioNet content URL is the download point for this release, the Synapse URL is the controlled-access route for raw audio, and the steps to qualify for each are spelled out.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: URLs are well-formed and the domains match the declared publisher and the stated controlled-access repository. Flagged as a low-severity slot-placement completeness issue rather than an absence of information.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: 'Parquet' (dense binary feature files, loadable by any Parquet library) and 'Tab-separated values with JSON data dictionaries'; file_collections names the nine Parquet feature files individually (ppgs.parquet, sparc_ema.parquet, sparc_loudness.parquet, sparc_periodicity.parquet, sparc_pitch.parquet, torchaudio_spectrogram.parquet, torchaudio_mfcc.parquet, torchaudio_pitch.parquet, torchaudio_mel_spectrogram.parquet) plus static_features.tsv and audio_quality_metrics.tsv
sub_elements.quality_note: Formats are specific, standard, and resolved to the level of individual file names, with the pairing convention (each file accompanied by a JSON data dictionary sharing its stem) stated explicitly.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Formats are appropriate to the content: columnar Parquet for dense time-varying tensors, delimited text for per-recording tables. MIME types and character encoding are not declared, a minor gap that does not obscure the file types.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets with four typed, DOI- or accession-identified targets; external_resources listing docs.b2ai-voice.org, github.com/sensein/b2aiprep (Apache-2.0), github.com/sensein/senselab, github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap (MIT), github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs (MIT), and the Synapse raw-audio location, with future_guarantees and access restrictions stated
sub_elements.quality_note: Links are numerous, typed, licensed where applicable, and accompanied by an explicit statement that they are supporting materials rather than dependencies because the dataset is self-contained — which tells a user what breaks if a link rots.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: All URLs are structurally valid with plausible domains. The restrictions attached to the Synapse link are consistent with the controlled-access policy stated in license_and_use_terms and third_party_sharing.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on fields outside this sub-element: distribution_formats populated with Parquet and TSV, access_urls pointing to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/, third_party_sharing.is_shared true.
sub_elements.evidence: license: Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: general_research_use; 'intended solely for commercial and non-commercial research purposes by Authorized Researchers; the consent does not restrict use to non-commercial purposes, to a geographic location, to a type of research, to genetic research, or away from methods and algorithm development'
sub_elements.quality_note: Reuse permissions are stated affirmatively and with the unusual precision of naming what is not restricted, which is what a downstream reuser actually needs in order to clear a project. The per-organization application requirement is also stated.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The permission enum, the prose terms and the consent scope agree; the license is bespoke rather than a standard CC instrument, which is disclosed rather than misrepresented as an open license.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated, PhysioNet access URL present, research-use license in force.
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: Parquet ('an open-source column-oriented data file format, and can be loaded with any library that supports Parquet') and tab-delimited plain text with companion JSON data dictionaries whose keys match the table column names
sub_elements.quality_note: All three formats used (Parquet, TSV, JSON) are open, widely supported and appropriate to their content, and the dictionary-to-table key correspondence is a genuine interoperability affordance rather than a nominal claim.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Character encoding is not declared for the delimited text, the one gap in this sub-element; format standardization itself is unambiguous and machine-actionable.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: Parquet/TSV distribution with PhysioNet access URLs and a research-use license.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry ontology term identifiers (B2AI_TOPIC:36, B2AI_TOPIC:37, B2AI_TOPIC:31, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:80); labeling_strategies.data_annotation_protocol: 'Labeling followed the Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10 codes'
sub_elements.quality_note: A resolvable schema URI with a named class, plus controlled-vocabulary term identifiers on instances and an ICD-10 coding statement for diagnostic labels. Scored on the source rubric's field pair (conforms_to, conforms_to_schema), of which the second is populated with a genuine schema.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Semantic caveat recorded: conforms_to_schema governs this metadata record rather than the released data tables, and conforms_to is deliberately omitted because the BIDS 1.9.0 conversion applies to the audio dataset's layout, not this feature-only release. The ontology term IDs and ICD-10 statement are what carry data-level conformance here, and they are thinner than the schema URI suggests. This same omission is scored against Element 10 sub-element 3, whose source-rubric field list is conforms_to alone.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats and PhysioNet access URLs populated.
sub_elements.evidence: variables: participant_id (identifier, is_identifier true), session_id (identifier, is_identifier true, 'A participant may have more than one session'), task_name (categorical), n_frames (integer); file_collections states every table is 'paired with a JSON data dictionary whose entries carry a description, the question put to the participant where there was one, and the data type of the response'
sub_elements.quality_note: The variables actually declared are the join keys that make the release integrable — participant_id, session_id and task_name are precisely what links feature tensors to metadata to phenotype rows, and relationships restates that linkage explicitly. Coverage of analytic columns is thin relative to the dozens of distributed tables, but the record names the authoritative source for those (the shipped JSON dictionaries) rather than leaving them undocumented.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Identifier flags are used correctly and the cardinality caveat (a participant may appear on multiple rows because sessions repeat, and responses need not agree across sessions) is a substantive integration warning. Thin coverage recorded as a low-severity completeness issue.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: three categories (clinical ML research, AI model pretraining/fine-tuning, voice biomarker research) with examples and usage notes; prohibited_uses: four (re-identification attempts, foreseeable harm or stigmatization, IP protections that restrict access, contacting subjects without IRB approval and written provider approval); discouraged_uses: two (non-research applications such as hiring, insurance pricing and surveillance; uses assuming representativeness)
sub_elements.quality_note: All three registers are populated, each with reasons attached rather than bare prohibitions, and the discouraged-uses entries connect directly to documented properties of the data (the skews recorded in subpopulations and known_biases).
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Prohibitions are consistent with the Registered Access Agreement described in license_and_use_terms and with the re-identification risk assessed in participant_privacy; no permission granted here contradicts a restriction stated elsewhere.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition met on E1 evidence: description states 'data for 833 adult participants recruited across five sites in North America' with clinical diagnoses established by clinicians. Governance condition independently met on E2 evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted' with credentialed access and a Certificate of Confidentiality. Determined without reference to any Element 4 field.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: reviewing_organization 'University of South Florida Institutional Review Board', review_details noting US sites joined through the Single IRB process with subsite approvals; human_subject_research.ethics_review_board and irb_approval repeating the approval and recording that the study is not for a drug or device and no data monitoring committee was appointed; governance contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org
sub_elements.quality_note: Oversight is named at the institution level, the mechanism (single IRB with subsite approvals) is identified, and the scope of approval covers both collection and sharing. The absence of a formal DPIA is the only gap in an otherwise complete oversight record.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects is true and IRB approval is populated, as required. data_protection_impacts is absent, but its substance is partly carried by participant_privacy.reidentification_risk, which is assessed rather than omitted.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same external evidence: human participants identified in description (E1); governance constraint stated in regulatory_restrictions and confidentiality_level (E2). Not determined from is_deidentified itself.
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.method: 'HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification, supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers and of highly sensitive non-identifying elements, and by withholding the raw audio waveform'; identifiers_removed enumerates eighteen categories including names, geographic locators, sub-year dates, SSNs, MRNs, device and biometric identifiers, with country retained; deidentification_details adds transcript review, removal of recordings with identifying information or external voices, date rebasing, narrative-field removal, and the disclosure that 'k-anonymization with k of at least two was not achieved'
sub_elements.quality_note: One of the strongest sub-elements in the record: a named standard, an enumerated identifier list, the supplementary measures beyond the standard, and an explicit statement of a de-identification guarantee that was *not* achieved. Negative disclosure of that kind is rare and materially useful.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Method appropriateness check passes: for biometric voice data, Safe Harbor alone would be insufficient, and the record's primary control is withholding the waveform and releasing derived features — a measure matched to the actual re-identification vector it names.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition met on E1 description ('833 adult participants', clinical cohorts) and on E8 collection_mechanisms, which describes in-clinic recruitment and administration of surveys to participants. Participants exist, so the sub-element has a subject matter.
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy.anonymization_method (Safe Harbor identifiers plus indirect/sensitive field removal, derived features in place of waveforms); privacy_techniques (controlled-access raw audio, manual transcript review, password-protected REDCap behind institutional HIPAA firewall, access limited to HIPAA-trained approved personnel, HTTPS transmission to HIPAA-compliant NIH STRIDES cloud storage); reidentification_risk ('a person's voice is unique to them and to their health at that time, so it is always possible, even if unlikely, that someone could recognize a participant by voice'); data_linkage (EHR access for gold-standard validation; linking datasheets kept within collecting institutions)
sub_elements.quality_note: Protections are described at both the technical and the administrative layer, and the risk assessment is honest about residual risk rather than declaring it eliminated. The linkage disclosure tells a user exactly what identifiable material exists and where it stays.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistency check passes: where a re-identification vector is named, a corresponding mitigation is named (waveform exclusion, prohibition on re-identification in prohibited_uses). Risk level stated is plausible for feature-only release of biometric-derived data.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition met on E1 description and E8 collection_mechanisms (in-clinic prospective collection from recruited participants).
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true; consent_type covering paper signature, in-app or REDCap electronic consent, and a video consent in which the participant reads a statement aloud (also used to verify the acoustic data belongs to the consented individual); consent_documentation (paper uploads stored in REDCap, retained at least five years); consent_scope (sharing of non-directly-identifying data, registered vs controlled access tiers, EHR access permission, re-consent before each longitudinal session); withdrawal_mechanism (withdrawal any time; data excluded if withdrawal precedes completion; recordings cannot be removed after collection completes); plus collection_consents, collection_notifications and consent_revocations corroborating
sub_elements.quality_note: Consent is documented end to end — modality, documentation, retention, scope, re-consent and the precise boundary at which withdrawal stops being effective. That last point is the one most datasheets omit and the one participants and reusers most need.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistency check passes: IRB approval documented and consent procedures documented together. The consent scope's permission of commercial research matches the license terms; the tiered-sharing language matches the actual two-tier access model.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition met on E1 description and E8 collection_mechanisms; the cohort definition in description names neurological, neurodegenerative and psychiatric conditions, so at-risk groups are within scope.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Data collection identified (acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms populated) AND datasets-shared condition met (Parquet/TSV distribution with PhysioNet access URLs).
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: the Bridge2AI-Voice tablet application ('Data were collected on iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) using an Avid AE-36 microphone connected through an Apple dongle', head-mounted where possible, collecting breathing and cough sounds, voice, speech and linguistic tasks plus surveys) and REDCap for clinical, diagnostic and questionnaire capture; direct_collection records in-clinic collection in the United States and Canada; data_collectors describes site research teams and site clinicians with their roles
sub_elements.quality_note: Hardware down to device generation and microphone model, the software stack, the setting, the personnel and their roles are all specified — enough for a reader to judge comparability with another corpus or to attempt replication.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Device specificity is what makes the measurement-bias disclosure in known_biases verifiable (distinct iPads per site, variable headset distance); collection description and bias description are mutually consistent.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same condition pair: collection identified in E8 fields and datasets shared per E2 distribution evidence.
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods with was_directly_observed, was_reported_by_subjects, was_inferred_derived and was_validated_verified all true, and acquisition_details distinguishing directly observed acoustic tasks, self-reported demographics and questionnaires, clinician-verified diagnoses, and the derived character of the released values ('features computed from the recorded waveforms rather than the waveforms themselves'); raw_sources identifying the REDCap and audio origins with a Synapse access URL

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Software-output condition met on E10/E2 evidence: external_resources references code repositories (github.com/sensein/b2aiprep under Apache-2.0, github.com/sensein/senselab, github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap under MIT). Determined without reference to E8's own preprocessing fields.
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: monaural conversion and 16 kHz resampling with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter; STFT with 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, downsampled by two in time for 201 frequency bins; 60 MFCCs and a 60-bin Mel spectrogram; SPARC kinematic traces for six articulators with loudness, periodicity and pitch at 50 Hz; PPGs over forty phoneme categories at 100 Hz; Whisper Large transcription; b2aiprep 3.0.0 and senselab. cleaning_strategies: an audit protocol generating missingness tables, checking distributions and outliers, validating categorical responses against the schema, and running audio QC on silence, duration and passage fidelity. labeling_strategies: clinician diagnosis with cohort-specific gold standards (laryngoscopy and stroboscopy, spirometry and flow-volume loops, brain CT and MRI, EHR plus psychiatrist diagnosis and medication history), annotations_per_item 1, annotator demographics, protocol and platform. machine_annotation_tools.tool_accuracy: off-the-shelf models such as transcription 'have not been audited for correctness'
sub_elements.quality_note: The strongest element in the record. Parameters are given at the level a reimplementation would need, cleaning is described as an auditable protocol, labeling includes the gold standard per cohort, and annotation quality is stated honestly including its unaudited components and the single-labeler limitation.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Signal-processing parameters are internally coherent (25 ms window at 16 kHz with a 400-point FFT gives the stated 201 bins). The healthsheet's 'No' answer to preprocessing-for-cleaning is disclosed in source_caveats as contradicted by the audit steps recorded elsewhere — surfaced rather than suppressed.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Element 8's datasets-shared gate is met and the release was processed (preprocessing_strategies and machine_annotation_tools establish transformation of the distributed data), so this sub-element is scored and is not gated on whether a repository is pointed at (#1081).
sub_elements.evidence: Evidence carried by machine_annotation_tools.tools (OpenAI Whisper Large; openSMILE; Praat via parselmouth; torchaudio; Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc); phonetic posteriorgrams (ppgs); b2aiprep; senselab) with per-tool descriptions of what each produced, corroborated by preprocessing_strategies ('Processing was performed with the b2aiprep library, version 3.0.0 for this release, and the senselab audio processing toolkit') and by external_resources, which gives repository URLs and licenses for b2aiprep and senselab
sub_elements.quality_note: Every named tool is in a producing or transforming role for the data actually distributed: torchaudio produced the spectrogram, Mel spectrogram, MFCC and pitch Parquet files; sparc produced the articulatory, loudness, periodicity and pitch tensors; ppgs produced the posteriorgrams; openSMILE and Praat/parselmouth produced static_features.tsv; b2aiprep and senselab orchestrated the pipeline and merged the phenotype files. A version is pinned for b2aiprep (3.0.0) and repositories are linked for the two consortium libraries, exceeding the naming threshold.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Threshold check passes on producing/transforming software, not on excluded roles: the tablet application (capture, role a), PhysioNet (hosting, role b) and REDCap (capture and label recording, role a) are also documented but were not relied on for this score. Tool-to-output mapping is verifiable against the nine Parquet file names in file_collections.

sub_elements.name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (distribution_formats and PhysioNet access URLs populated).
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: project documentation at docs.b2ai-voice.org (protocols, healthsheet, study metadata, AI-readiness assessment), b2aiprep (Apache-2.0), senselab, bridge2ai-redcap (MIT), bridge2ai-docs (MIT), Synapse raw audio, each with future_guarantees and access restrictions; missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy: 'Missing values are left as missing rather than imputed', with a missingness table distributed alongside the data
sub_elements.quality_note: External materials are numerous, licensed, typed by purpose and accompanied by an honest statement that no persistence guarantee is offered and that they are supporting rather than load-bearing. The imputation question is answered in the negative explicitly, which is the documented answer the sub-element accepts.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The imputation_protocols slot is unused; its substance is carried by missing_data_documentation, which states non-imputation rather than leaving it unaddressed. conforms_to is absent, with the BIDS scoping reason disclosed. Standards coverage is therefore the weakest of the three strands here but the sub-element is satisfied by resources and the imputation statement.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: five typed entries — coverage_limitation (fluent English speakers only, non-English speakers excluded, with Spanish protocols noted as under development and a source caveat about IRB revisions); representativeness_limitation (non-probability sample from high-volume expert clinics at five sites, with scope_impact on generalization); scope_limitation (derived features only, waveform analyses impossible on this release, mitigated by controlled-access raw audio); temporal_limitation (protocol changed over the study, diagnostic practice drift as a source of distribution shift); coverage_limitation (unequal disease-category distribution, pediatric category omitted, multimodal imaging/genomic/respiratory data not included)
sub_elements.quality_note: Limitations are typed, each carries a described consequence, and three carry recommended mitigations. The set covers language, sampling, modality scope, time and content coverage — no obvious dimension is left unaddressed.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Each limitation is corroborated elsewhere: the sampling limitation by sampling_strategies, the scope limitation by raw_sources and description, the coverage limitation by subpopulations and related_datasets (pediatric released separately). No limitation contradicts a capability claimed in intended_uses.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases with bias_type values selection_bias, representation_bias, measurement_bias and annotation_bias, each with a bias_description and, for the first three, a mitigation_strategy or affected_subsets ('Disease cohort categories, which are confounded with collection site and device'); future_use_impacts adds two downstream impact statements on multivariate skew and on models learning site or device signatures
sub_elements.quality_note: Four distinct taxonomy categories are used correctly rather than as synonyms, and the measurement-bias entry identifies a genuine and non-obvious confound between cohort, site and recording device. The social-impact strand required by the RAI alignment is carried by future_use_impacts.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Bias types map to recognizable BiasTypeEnum categories. The representation-bias description (five sites in the US and Canada, fluent English only) is numerically consistent with the description and known_limitations; the annotation-bias entry is consistent with labeling_strategies.annotations_per_item of 1.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: four entries covering differing site configurations and a protocol that changed over the study; noise artifacts, inter-site variation in diagnostic practice, inaccurate questionnaire responses and underreporting; unaudited off-the-shelf models for derived products such as transcription; and audio files that could not yield certain features and are absent from the corresponding bundled files
sub_elements.quality_note: Anomalies are concrete and each has a traceable effect on the released artifact — the last one directly explains the unequal per-feature record counts reported in instances.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Anomaly set is consistent with missing_data_documentation.missing_data_causes and with the per-feature count discrepancies; the record does not claim a data quality it elsewhere disclaims (the notes even report the AI-readiness self-assessment scoring Characterization 80 percent 'with the data quality criterion not met').

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present true, with race and ethnic origin, sexual orientation, socioeconomic and health information named and the observation that 'Voice itself is a biometric characteristic; the derived features are released in place of the waveform for that reason', plus a source_caveat recording the conflict with the version 3.0.0 removal account; content_warnings: content_warnings_present false with a warning text explaining that the healthsheet's offensive-language warning concerns free-speech transcripts removed at 1.1 and excluded from the feature-only 3.0.0/3.1.0 releases
sub_elements.quality_note: Sensitive attributes are enumerated, the biometric rationale for the release design is stated, and the superseded content warning is carried with an explanation of why it no longer applies rather than being silently dropped.

Both are disclosed by the record itself, so the user is not misled; they are reported as issues rather than scored against this sub-element, whose substance is amply present.

sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: USF IRB review of collection and sharing, with US sites joining through the Single IRB process and subsite approvals; future_use_impacts: skews by disorder category, site and demographics with the warning to consider the multivariate distribution 'to avoid unfair treatment of individuals or groups through stereotyping or quality-of-service failures', and the risk that models learn site or device signatures rather than disease signatures; discouraged_uses names hiring, insurance pricing and surveillance as harms to avoid

The social-impact statements are consistent with known_biases and with the prohibitions in prohibited_uses, and the ethics review is the same one recorded in Element 4 sub-element 1, used here for its social-impact pairing rather than duplicated as new evidence.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (Parquet/TSV distribution with PhysioNet access URLs).
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to is absent. source_caveats states: 'the BIDS version 1.9.0 conversion described in the project documentation concerns the audio dataset's folder layout, and is noted in raw_sources rather than asserted as a property of this release, which is why conforms_to and conforms_to_standard are omitted.' The only standards signals for the released artifact are ICD-10 mentioned within labeling_strategies.data_annotation_protocol and conforms_to_schema, which declares the datasheet's own schema rather than the data's.
sub_elements.quality_note: No community data standard is claimed for this release. The omission is deliberate and honestly reasoned — asserting BIDS conformance would have been inaccurate for a feature-only release — but the sub-element asks whether the dataset connects to community standards, and for the distributed tables the answer given is effectively none. A reader cannot determine whether the phenotype tables follow any shared clinical data model (OMOP, FHIR, CDISC) or only a project-internal convention.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Scored strictly on the source rubric's field for this item (conforms_to), which is empty. Element 3 sub-element 3 scores 1 because its field list also admits conforms_to_schema, which is populated; the divergence is deliberate and reflects the two items' different scopes, data-level standards here versus schema conformance there.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met.
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://b2ai-voice.org/; external_resources: docs.b2ai-voice.org carrying protocols, healthsheet, study metadata and AI-readiness assessment, plus four public code repositories with licenses; existing_uses notes the Bridge2AI Summer School and hackathon and lists training opportunities at https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/; extension_mechanism.contribution_url https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep with discussion forums, issue pages and pull requests accepted
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation, training and community-contribution channels are all linked, and the contribution route is described operationally (forums, issues, pull requests against the preprocessing code), which is genuine ecosystem integration rather than a bare homepage.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: All URLs are well-formed with plausible domains consistent with the project and its GitHub organizations (sensein, eipm). The scholars and summer-school references corroborate the outreach claim with concrete instances.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met.
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_supplemented_by 10.13026/h995-bt35 (pediatric dataset v1.1.0, 23,533 recordings from 300 participants aged 2-18 at SickKids under REB approval, raw audio at syn73617068); is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68 (v3.0.0, published 16 December 2025); is_version_of 10.13026/37yb-1t42 (concept DOI); derives_from syn72370534 (adult raw audio under controlled access)
sub_elements.quality_note: Four relationships, each typed with a standard vocabulary term, each pointing at a resolvable identifier, and each annotated with enough detail (counts, sites, ethics approval, access route) for a user to decide whether to pursue it.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship semantics are used correctly and the targets are mutually consistent: the pediatric companion is supplementary rather than a version, the immediate predecessor is a version predecessor, and the raw audio is a derivation source, matching was_derived_from and raw_sources.

strengths: Ethics and privacy documentation is complete and internally coherent across the whole chain: USF single-IRB approval with subsite approvals, three consent modalities with an explicitly stated withdrawal boundary, HIPAA Safe Harbor plus indirect-identifier removal, an honest re-identification risk assessment grounded in the biometric nature of voice, and the disclosure that k-anonymity with k>=2 was not achieved.

The release design is legible: the record states repeatedly and consistently that only derived features are distributed, why (voice is biometric), where the withheld waveforms live (Synapse, syn72370534), and what it costs the user (waveform analyses are impossible on this release), rather than obscuring the omission.

Processing is documented at replicable granularity — 16 kHz monaural resampling with a Butterworth filter, STFT at 25 ms/10 ms/400-point giving 201 bins, 60 MFCCs, SPARC at 50 Hz, PPGs over forty phonemes at 100 Hz — with the producing software named per output and b2aiprep pinned to version 3.0.0.

Source conflicts are disclosed rather than resolved silently: grant identifier variants, participant and target counts, language eligibility, the access model across releases, and the healthsheet's contradiction of the cleaning account each carry a source_caveats entry naming the disagreeing sources and the preference rule applied.

Limitations, biases and anomalies are typed, specific and causally connected: the measurement-bias entry identifies that disease cohort is confounded with site and therefore with recording device, and future_use_impacts follows that through to the concrete modeling risk of learning site signatures rather than disease signatures.

Version and provenance tracking is thorough — six releases with dates and contents, three errata naming breaking changes such as renamed gold-standard variables, per-version DOIs plus a concept DOI, and an explicit note that version 1.1 files have been withdrawn.
weaknesses: Keywords are the record's weakest field by a wide margin: four broad terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice) for a dataset whose own phenotype directory names eighteen clinical conditions and whose features span six distinct acoustic representations. Discovery by condition, modality or method is not supported.

No community data standard is asserted for the released artifact. conforms_to is deliberately omitted because BIDS applies to the audio layout rather than this release, leaving the phenotype tables' conformance to any shared clinical data model undocumented.

The stated semi-annual update cadence is contradicted by the record's own release history of five releases in roughly sixteen months, and version_access.latest_version_doi holds the concept DOI rather than the DOI of the version described.

variables declares only four elements — the join keys — for a release containing dozens of phenotype tables; the authoritative variable metadata is deferred to the shipped JSON data dictionaries without a field explicitly saying so.

Several canonical slots are left empty while their content sits elsewhere: download_url (access URLs live in distribution_formats), at_risk_populations (content in human_subject_research.special_populations), imputation_protocols (non-imputation stated in missing_data_documentation), data_protection_impacts, and is_tabular.

Two flag-versus-content pairings read as contradictory on a shallow machine reading: content_warnings_present false with a populated warnings list, and confidential_elements_present false for a release that is credentialed, covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality and characterized as PII in its transfer agreement.
recommendations: Expand keywords to eight or more terms drawn from content already in the record — the principal conditions (Parkinson's disease, ALS, laryngeal cancer, depression, chronic cough), the feature types (spectrogram, MFCC, phonetic posteriorgram, articulatory), and the design (adult cohort, clinical voice recordings).

Populate conforms_to with whatever standard the released tables do follow, scoped to this release — for example ICD-10 coding of the diagnosis columns and the table-plus-JSON-dictionary convention — so the omission of BIDS does not leave the standards question blank.

Correct version_access.latest_version_doi to the resolved version DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66, or annotate the value explicitly as the concept DOI, and restate updates.frequency against the observed PhysioNet release history rather than the Health Data Nexus plan.

Populate download_url with the PhysioNet content URL, at_risk_populations with the special_populations content, and imputation_protocols with the existing non-imputation statement, so machine consumers find these facts in their canonical slots.

Either expand variables to cover the principal analytic columns of the phenotype tables, or add an explicit statement that the distributed JSON data dictionaries are the authoritative variable metadata for this release.

Resolve the sensitive-element conflict against the 3.1.0 file inventory by listing which sensitive attributes actually remain in the released tables, and move the superseded free-speech content warning into a historical note so the content_warnings flag and its payload agree.
